title: Acute decompensated heart failure, 72-year-old woman
provenance: Vignette written 2026-09-30 for the evaluation harness; expected answers extracted from the cited documents.

intake.complaint: Increasing breathlessness over 3 days, now breathless lying flat, with swollen legs.
intake.history: Known heart failure. Has not taken her furosemide for a week. Diabetic.

triage.note: Both extractors: level 1. A: Primary triage Rapid Assessment, Respiratory Distress row: the Level 1 column (x~136, p4) lists 'SpO2 < 90% room air'; SpO2 89% meets it only if it was read on room air, which the intake does not say. If she was already on oxygen, the most urgent cell is the adult Vital Signs Level 2 column (x~131, p7) 'SpO2 < 92%'. 'Need O2 support' (p4, x~356) is Level 3; HR 112 and RR 28 are Level 3 on p7. Level 1 is expected (worst applicable cell, MTS p7 higher-level rule). Level 2 is acceptable. B: SpO2 89% is taken as a room-air reading, which falls in the Level 1 Rapid Assessment cell 'SpO2 < 90% room air' (x~136, p4). If the reading was on oxygen or the cell is judged not to apply, the adult vital-signs cell 'SpO2 < 92%' (x~131, p7) gives Level 2. HR 112 and RR 28 are Level 3 cells (x~244); the intake's 'needs O2 support' is a Level 3 cell (x~356, p4). The most urgent applicable cell is chosen.

disposition.note: Admit. ICU/CCU/HDU if SpO2 stays < 90% on supplemental oxygen, she needs NIV or invasive ventilation, or there is hypoperfusion, arrhythmia or haemodynamic instability. Otherwise HDU or ward. / Admission is certain. ICU/CCU/HDU is preferred because she is hypoxic (89%) with RR 28 and is a likely NIV candidate. A general ward is acceptable if SpO2 corrects on oxygen and there is no hypoperfusion. RESUSCITATION_BAY is accepted only as the initial ED zone, because the MTS triage level is 1.

adjudication.method: two independent extraction passes (A, B); agreed items scored

A: Triage: Level 1 depends on the SpO2 of 89% being a room-air reading, which the intake does not state. If she was on oxygen, it is Level 2.

Disposition preferred: ward vs HDU/CCU depends on her response to oxygen and diuretic. The CPG puts HDU and ward together for patients who are not high-risk. I chose ADMIT_WARD as preferred; ADMIT_ICU_HDU is equally defensible if NIV is started.
The HF CPG gives no single ED dose of GTN for this BP (168/96); nitrates are listed only as optional.
The CCB avoidance (diltiazem/verapamil/nifedipine) is stated for HFrEF. Her ejection fraction is unknown.
B: Is SpO2 89% a room-air reading? This decides MTS Level 1 ('SpO2 < 90% room air') versus Level 2 ('SpO2 < 92%').
LVEF is unknown. The CPG's advice to avoid diltiazem/verapamil/nifedipine is written for HFrEF, so that item is non-required.
Morphine: the CPG says routine use 'cannot be recommended' but does not forbid it, so it is left out of drugs_forbidden.
